request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: tiled stove (kachelofen) with cast iron door
remains of a brick fireplace or oven in the background
debris-covered floor of a burned-out room

damaged_parts.condition: burned, partly collapsed and hanging diagonally
covered with ash, charred timber and debris
soot-blackened on sides, some tiles missing or broken, but largely intact
burned through, leaving an open gap to the next room

visible_items: white tiled stove with iron firing door
wheelbarrow or metal tub lying tilted
regional_indicators: tiled stove and log construction typical of Northern or Eastern European houses
parsed_output.summary_en: A burned-out interior of a log-built room is shown, with heavily charred walls, collapsed beams and a floor covered in ash and debris. A white tiled stove with an iron door stands on the left, soot-stained but mostly intact.
